subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A surgeon is reviewing the ligaments of the liver before a procedure. One ligament connects the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and is a derivative of the ventral mesentery.
question: Which structure is contained within the falciform ligament?
explanation_correct: The falciform ligament connects the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and is a derivative of the ventral mesentery. It contains the ligamentum teres hepatis, the remnant of the fetal umbilical vein, along with patent paraumbilical veins. These paraumbilical veins can become dilated portosystemic collaterals in portal hypertension, producing caput medusae. Distinguishing the falciform contents from the portal triad is a common anatomy test point.

explanation_incorrect.A: The proper hepatic artery is part of the portal triad within the hepatoduodenal ligament.
explanation_incorrect.C: The common bile duct is part of the portal triad in the hepatoduodenal ligament.
explanation_incorrect.D: Short gastric vessels run within the gastrosplenic ligament.
explanation_incorrect.E: The splenic artery runs within the splenorenal ligament.

educationalObjective: The falciform ligament contains the ligamentum teres (fetal umbilical vein remnant) and is a ventral mesentery derivative.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: During a hepatic resection, the surgeon places a clamp on the hepatoduodenal ligament within the omental foramen to control bleeding from the liver.
question: Which three structures make up the portal triad contained in this ligament?

options.text: Proper hepatic artery, hepatic vein, and common bile duct
Portal vein, hepatic vein, and inferior vena cava
Proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct
Left gastric artery, portal vein, and common hepatic duct
Superior mesenteric artery, splenic vein, and common bile duct

explanation_correct: The hepatoduodenal ligament contains the portal triad: the proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct. Compressing this ligament in the omental foramen (the Pringle maneuver) controls inflow to the liver from the portal vein and hepatic artery, as opposed to outflow through the hepatic veins and IVC. The ligament also borders the omental foramen, which connects the greater and lesser sacs, and is part of the lesser omentum.

explanation_incorrect.A: The hepatic vein is not part of the portal triad; it drains into the IVC.
explanation_incorrect.B: The hepatic vein and IVC represent outflow, not the portal triad of the hepatoduodenal ligament.
explanation_incorrect.D: The left gastric artery runs in the hepatogastric ligament, not within the portal triad.
explanation_incorrect.E: The superior mesenteric artery and splenic vein are not components of the portal triad.

educationalObjective: The portal triad (proper hepatic artery, portal vein, common bile duct) lies in the hepatoduodenal ligament; the Pringle maneuver compresses it.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A surgeon needs to enter the lesser sac to inspect the posterior stomach. She divides a ligament that connects the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach and separates the greater and lesser sacs on the right.
question: Which ligament did she divide, and what vessels does it contain?
explanation_correct: The hepatogastric ligament connects the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach. It contains gastric vessels, is a ventral mesentery derivative, and is part of the lesser omentum. It separates the greater and lesser sacs on the right and may be cut during surgery to access the lesser sac. This contrasts with the gastrosplenic ligament, which separates the sacs on the left.

explanation_incorrect.A: The gastrocolic ligament connects the greater curvature to the transverse colon and is part of the greater omentum.
explanation_incorrect.B: The gastrosplenic ligament connects the greater curvature to the spleen and separates the sacs on the left, not the right.
explanation_incorrect.C: The hepatoduodenal ligament contains the portal triad and borders the omental foramen, not the attachment to the lesser curvature.
explanation_incorrect.E: The splenorenal ligament connects the spleen to the left pararenal space and contains splenic vessels and the pancreatic tail.

educationalObjective: The hepatogastric ligament links liver to lesser curvature, carries gastric vessels, and may be divided to access the lesser sac.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A patient with gastric cancer undergoes evaluation of the greater omentum. The surgeon identifies a ligament connecting the greater curvature of the stomach to the spleen, which separates the greater and lesser sacs on the left.
question: Which vessels run within this ligament?

options.text: Short gastrics and left gastroepiploic vessels
Right gastric and right gastroepiploic vessels only
Splenic artery and vein and tail of pancreas

explanation_correct: The gastrosplenic ligament connects the greater curvature of the stomach to the spleen. It contains the short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels, is derived from the dorsal mesentery, and is part of the greater omentum. It separates the greater and lesser sacs on the left. This is a classic distinction from the gastrocolic ligament (gastroepiploic arteries to the transverse colon) and the splenorenal ligament (splenic vessels and pancreatic tail).

explanation_incorrect.B: Right gastric and right gastroepiploic vessels are not the contents of the gastrosplenic ligament.
explanation_incorrect.C: The portal triad is located within the hepatoduodenal ligament.
explanation_incorrect.D: Splenic vessels and the pancreatic tail are found in the splenorenal ligament, not the gastrosplenic ligament.
explanation_incorrect.E: The ligamentum teres and paraumbilical veins are contents of the falciform ligament.

educationalObjective: The gastrosplenic ligament carries short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels and separates the greater and lesser sacs on the left.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: During a splenectomy, the surgeon divides the ligament that attaches the spleen to the left pararenal space. She is careful to identify nearby structures that may be injured within it.
question: Which structures are contained in the splenorenal ligament?

options.text: Short gastric vessels and left gastroepiploic vessels
Proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct
Splenic artery and vein, and the tail of the pancreas

explanation_correct: The splenorenal ligament connects the spleen to the left pararenal space. It is a derivative of the dorsal mesentery and contains the splenic artery and vein along with the tail of the pancreas. Injury to the splenic artery or the pancreatic tail during splenectomy is a well-known complication. The presence of the pancreatic tail is the high-yield association for this ligament.

explanation_incorrect.A: Short gastrics and left gastroepiploic vessels run within the gastrosplenic ligament.
explanation_incorrect.B: Gastroepiploic arteries run in the gastrocolic and gastrosplenic ligaments.
explanation_incorrect.C: The portal triad is contained within the hepatoduodenal ligament.
explanation_incorrect.D: The ligamentum teres hepatis is contained within the falciform ligament.

educationalObjective: The splenorenal ligament contains the splenic artery and vein and the tail of the pancreas.
